findings.claim: GetEqualityComparer for untrusted data now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing TypeAccessException for types with no hash-resistant comparer. This silently disables the hash-collision DoS protection for UntrustedData, a security regression unrelated to the requirement. The hunk contradicts the file's own comment, which says non-whitelisted types must not be allowed as hash keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKeyType,int> with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. Base throws TypeAccessException; head succeeds with the default comparer. Assert that TypeAccessException is thrown.

findings.claim: The requirement says that if T carries [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[DataContract] attributes they are honoured. The collector never reads attributes on T. It always uses contractless name-sorted mode, or the surrogate. A T with [Key(n)] int keys or [IgnoreMember] gets a different wire format than the standard generated formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Take T with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] on its members. Serialize with the existing generated formatter (array form), then with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class for T. Compare the bytes; they differ (map vs array).

findings.claim: Contractless mode skips get-only members, includes only public read-write members, and sorts them by name. This differs from ContractlessStandardResolver, which uses declaration order and handles read-only members. Anyone already serializing with the contractless resolver would see a different wire order and fewer members after switching to the generated formatter. Ledger L22 accepts this.

receipt_plan.detail: L22 accepts name-sorted, read-write-only output, so this is not a defect.

findings.claim: New Error-severity diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added to SupportedDiagnostics. However, the analyzer never reports them. They are reported only from a generator through RegisterSourceOutput. AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md is not updated, so RS2000 release-tracking warnings fire. Because the diagnostics come from the generator, the analyzer descriptors are also inconsistent. No help docs exist for the new ids.

receipt_plan.detail: Build the SourceGenerator project and check for RS2000 (analyzer release tracking) warnings on MsgPack019-022. Run the analyzer tests on a non-partial [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class and assert that the diagnostic is reported.

findings.claim: The generator filter uses a string comparison on the attribute class's ToDisplayString. This is fine, but the generator now also treats any class with the attribute as non-hand-written. For existing users nothing changes unless they opt in. A rejected formatter that is silently dropped from the resolver could also drop a working hand-written formatter registration.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratorUtilities.cs:35-40. A class with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] that fails validation is excluded from both paths.
